correctness.rationale: The exact finite theorem dFl(P31) ≃ wedge^960 S4 has been reconstructed for the ordinary unordered complex of transitive vertex subsets of the Paley tournament on Z/31, with residues explicitly verified. Independent fresh Python enumeration reproduced all 27,931 faces, dimension face vector (31,465,3255,9765,10695,3255,465), and all 126,015 nonempty Hasse covers. An independently coded repeated-toggle matching in the recorded 31-pivot order has 13,396 disjoint pairs and exactly one critical 0-cell, 89 critical 3-cells and 1,049 critical 4-cells. Independently built reversed-matched Hasse graph topologically sorted all 27,931 nodes, proving acyclicity. Independent signed boundary reduction gives D of shape 89x1049, 16,282 nonzero entries and |entry|<=8; exact ranks are 89 modulo 2,3,5,7,101,601. The 89 pivot columns selected modulo 2 have an exact Bareiss-equivalent determinant -601, while full rank modulo 601 means the greatest common divisor of maximal minors is coprime to 601, therefore equals 1. All nonzero integral Smith factors are 1, with free kernel rank 960. The CW model has cells only in dimensions 0,3,4; the 3-skeleton is wedge^89 S3, where Hurewicz identifies pi3 with H3, and integral Smith changes of basis give a wedge^960 S4 homotopy cofiber. Finite exhaustive verification is sufficient for this fixed 31-vertex object, not a universal family. Independent code was kept separate from repository verify.py.
residual_risks: Enumeration and Morse boundary are finite but computation-intensive; independent implementation shares the underlying mathematics and input pivot sequence, so common conceptual mistakes are possible.

The abstract CW-to-homotopy inference uses standard Forman discrete Morse theory, Hurewicz in dimension three and integer changes of degree bases on wedge^89 S3; no Lean formalization or expert external attestation is asserted.

value.rationale: The Paley tournament P31 is a canonical quadratic-residue doubly regular tournament of the first permissible size beyond the completed 27-vertex DRT homotopy census. Unlike an arbitrary small-instance slice, this is a natural test object at the first uncovered order, where prior smaller doubly regular examples exhibit both torsion and mixed-dimensional Moore-space phenomena. The exact integral wedge multiplicity and full primitive Morse-boundary certificate provide a sharp benchmark and a reusable reference for tournament-topology comparisons. It is an exact finite invariant with motivation independent of an all-order theorem. It neither classifies every 31-vertex DRT nor implies all Paley orders are wedges.
residual_risks: The result is only for a single specified finite tournament and does not settle the full order-31 census or a general structural theorem; its value is the natural exact benchmark.

scientific_limitations: Only one finite Paley tournament, no all-order or all-DRT classification.
Deniz 2015 full text inaccessible through the attempted authorized routes; originality is best-of-knowledge with explicit residual risk.
No external formal certification is claimed.
